assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray and then optical and radio afterglows settled the long-standing question of where gamma-ray bursts come from. It fixed their distances and cosmological origin, and opened a whole field linking compact-object formation, relativistic jets and the high-redshift universe. It also rested on an instrument achievement: a wide-field camera paired with a rapid-pointing narrow-field X-ray payload on a satellite. As an instrument builder I value that very highly.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX GRB localisation and the first X-ray afterglow detection. Kulkarni led the follow-up that gave the first redshift and the radio afterglow. The supplied list fits a three-person prize. I know the optical detection involved other groups, and a key figure (van Paradijs) died in 1999 and cannot be considered. I am not certain how the optical and redshift credit should be divided.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. The result dates from 1997 and has been confirmed repeatedly by Swift, Fermi and ground-based follow-up. The cosmological distance scale and the link between long bursts and supernovae are solid. If anything the recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the BeppoSAX team and the optical and radio follow-up groups is contested, and I cannot verify the details independently.
The deceased pioneer and the large collaboration size could complicate a fair three-person configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by evidence for a blazar source (TXS 0506+056) and for the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy as a real observational window. It required a cubic-kilometre instrument built in Antarctic ice, a major detector achievement that fits the tradition of rewarding new ways of observing the Universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA. A single-laureate option is clean. I would note that the wider collaboration and other instrument leaders also made decisive contributions, and the supplied credit lists only him. A single name may under-represent the early experimental leadership.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature for the diffuse flux, which is confirmed in several analyses and by independent detectors in the Mediterranean and Lake Baikal. Source identification is still developing and the TXS 0506+056 association is a single-source result. The field is solid, but source physics is not yet complete.
uncertainties: Whether the supplied credit is sufficient, or whether others who built IceCube deserve inclusion, is not resolved.
Neutrino source identifications remain statistically modest, so the astrophysical interpretation may keep changing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and completed the Standard Model. The 2013 prize recognised the theory. The experimental achievement, including detectors of unprecedented scale and performance, has not been recognised. Its importance and clarity are beyond question.
assessment.attribution: The three names are the founding spokespeople and detector leaders of the two experiments. This is a defensible but imperfect proxy for a collaboration of thousands, with the Nobel rule limiting the number of laureates. Other individuals with decisive analysis, accelerator or detector roles will feel overlooked, and the committee has historically hesitated here.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The discovery dates from 2012, with detailed couplings measured over a decade. Recognition is timely and is a matter of settling a fair attribution rule.
uncertainties: Whether any three persons can fairly represent two collaborations, and whether the accelerator contribution should be reflected, remains unresolved.
I have not verified details of individual roles in the discovery analyses.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory prediction of flat bands at a magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states launched the moiré materials field. It is a rare theory-plus-experiment story with a large and growing literature.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 theory prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental breakthrough. The three-person split is natural, although Cory Dean, Pablo's collaborators and others made important related contributions that are not on the list. I defer to colleagues for fine allocation in condensed matter.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature but still evolving. Many groups have reproduced the correlated states, though the mechanism of superconductivity and sample-to-sample variability are still debated. Some may call recognition early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the role of sample disorder are not settled.
Condensed matter is outside my own expertise, so my confidence in the relative ranking of this field is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have found evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black hole binaries. This opens a new gravitational-wave band using the Galaxy as a detector. The patience and calibration work behind pulsar timing is exactly what I respect in an experiment.
assessment.attribution: The names represent NANOGrav, EPTA and PPTA, the three leading arrays. Decades of foundational timing work by many people contributes, so allocation is hard. The announced evidence was a coordinated multi-collaboration release in 2023.
assessment.maturity: Premature relative to others. The Hellings-Downs correlation evidence is at roughly 3 to 4 sigma in each array, and the source interpretation (supermassive binaries versus new physics) is not settled. Independent confirmation is arriving, but the result is not yet a firm detection.
uncertainties: The significance of the detection is still below the conventional discovery standard.
The astrophysical origin of the signal is unresolved, and credit across collaborations is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on the magic-wavelength proposal and its realisation with strontium atoms, bring fractional uncertainty to the 10^-18 level. They are the most precise measurement instruments ever built. They enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy, and prepare a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks. Jun Ye pushed the performance to record levels. This is a clean two-person attribution, although the Hall and Hänsch frequency comb prize (2005) and others have a closely related lineage, and the roles of Ye's wider community deserve scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Mature in technology, with several independent laboratories reaching comparable performance. The practical impact (redefinition of the second) is still pending, so timing could be argued either way.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition of optical frequency metrology and with ion-clock work could affect how the committee frames novelty.
I have not independently verified who first proposed each element of the lattice clock concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices have become a controllable platform for quantum many-body physics, allowing the Mott-insulator transition and quantum simulation of Hubbard models to be observed. The platform proposals by Cirac and Zoller joined with Bloch's and Greiner's experiments to create a new field.
assessment.attribution: The theory (Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators) and the experiments (Greiner, Bloch) form a natural split, but the supplied list has four names and a prize allows only three. Greiner's early Mott-insulator demonstration is arguably decisive, so leaving him out is a real cost. I would need colleagues to weigh the allocation between theory and experiment.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research field with many independent groups. The quantum-simulation payoff beyond what classical computers can do remains partly prospective.
uncertainties: Choosing three from four names, and whether the credit split between theory and experiment is balanced, is unresolved.
Overlap with the Bose-Einstein condensation prize (2001) and with trapped-ion and cold-atom quantum information work may complicate framing.
This is outside my main expertise, so I defer to atomic-physics colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The WMAP mapping of the cosmic microwave background gave precise measurements of the age, composition and geometry of the Universe and established the standard LambdaCDM model. It was a landmark satellite instrument and analysis programme that I find very persuasive on experimental grounds.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page led instrument design and calibration, and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. A natural trio, though many other WMAP team members and the preceding COBE and ground-based work complicate the credit. The Nobel prizes in 2006 (COBE) and 2019 (cosmology) have already covered nearby ground.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and independently confirmed and extended by Planck. The risk is not maturity but that the Nobel committee may feel the cosmology area has recently been rewarded.
uncertainties: The overlap with earlier cosmology prizes could reduce its priority.
Whether instrument leadership or cosmological analysis should be weighted more is open.
